description:
We are the Pillars of Creation team, composed of students from the Technical Program in Administration at SENAI. We are very excited to participate in this NASA challenge!
We have a strong passion for project management, process analysis, strategy, and sustainable innovation, and we are ready to transform raw data and complex challenges into viable, well-structured, and high-impact proposals.
summary: Space Explorers is an interactive educational web game that transforms the history of space exploration into a journey of discovery and preservation. We developed a lightweight, browser-based experience where players pilot an astronaut to find and catalog 24 real probes, rovers, and spacecraft left behind on the Moon, Mars, and deep space. The project addresses the challenge by replacing static technical lists with engaging, gamified storytelling. By blending official NASA and JPL records with emotional reconstructions of each machine's "final transmission," alongside a virtual museum, interactive timeline, and quizzes, we give a human voice and context to historic missions. It is important because it democratizes access to humanity's off-world heritage, building an inspiring emotional bond between students, children, and space engineering to spark the curiosity of the next generation of explorers.
details:
Space Explorers: Abandoned, but not forgotten.
Team Pillars of Creation

1. Project Overview & Concept

Space Explorers is an interactive, browser-based educational game that preserves and humanizes the history of space exploration. Instead of presenting missions as static encyclopedia entries, it puts players in the role of an astronaut who launches from Earth, explores the Moon, Mars, and deep space, and finds 24 real spacecraft, landers, rovers, and instruments that NASA left behind, building a personal museum along the way.

2. How It Works & Key Features

Space Explorers is a lightweight, zero-installation web application built with HTML5 Canvas, CSS, and JavaScript. It runs on desktop (keyboard controls) and on mobile devices (on-screen touch controls). Its core features include:

  • Interactive 2D Exploration: Players take off from Earth, fly through the solar system, land on the Moon and Mars, and walk the surface to find iconic hardware such as the Surveyor landers, the Apollo Lunar Rovers, Spirit, Opportunity, Viking, Pioneer, and Voyager.
  • Investigation & Last Transmissions: In the Explorer Laboratory, players follow clues to work out why each piece of equipment went silent. Each one also has a “last transmission,” a short first-person educational reconstruction, and a Memorial where players can leave a message for it. This builds an emotional connection with the engineering and human effort behind each mission.
  • Virtual Museum of Abandoned Explorers: Every discovery is added to an interactive museum that can be browsed by destination (Moon, Mars, Deep Space), shows each mission’s operational status, and presents history, scientific discoveries, and fun facts for each piece.
  • Interactive Timeline & Progress System: A chronological timeline traces spaceflight from the 1960s onward, and a “Reverse time” tool shows when each piece of equipment was active, when it made its last contact, and how long it has been silent. Rank medals, a progress dashboard, and a shareable explorer card reward progress and reinforce learning.
  • Class Mode: Players can export a collection code and import classmates’ codes to build a shared collection.

3. Use of NASA Data & Scientific Accuracy

The mission histories, launch and landing dates, locations, operational statuses, and scientific discoveries in the catalog are based on records from NASA, the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), and the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA). Images come from the JPL Photojournal and the NASA Image and Video Library. A credits and sources section inside the game links to the primary NASA resources for further study and notes which elements are educational reconstructions (the last transmissions) or approximations (scale comparisons).

4. Impact & Future Potential

By combining scientific rigor with accessible game design, Space Explorers turns complex aerospace archives into an inspiring storytelling medium. It works as a free classroom and public-outreach tool that can spark curiosity about STEM and space heritage in young learners worldwide. Planned next steps include additional missions, multilingual support, and educator guides.

Space Explorers is an independent educational game and is not officially affiliated with NASA. Data: NASA / JPL / NSSDCA. Images: JPL Photojournal and NASA Image and Video Library.

GitHub repository: https://github.com/gustavo090708-lgtm/space-explorers
